clues: A megacity fills a high mountain basin more than two kilometers above the sea, ringed by volcanoes where a great lake once shimmered.
At this height the sun burns by day but nights stay cool all year — and the rainy season fires a thunderstorm nearly every afternoon.
An island city of canals and causeways stood here until 1521; the conquerors drained the lake and raised their churches on its stones.
Its great square sits over a buried temple, and the whole city is slowly sinking as the old lakebed settles beneath it.
The great cathedral and the national palace face each other across one of the world's largest plazas.
